_comment: Every Azure role GitOps Manager's runners get, read by setup-pipeline.ps1 step 12c (RUNNERS=1). This file is the list: setup grants what is here and nothing else.

Two identities: the runners (id-aksmanager-runners), which every workflow on gom-azure-adhoc / -long / -alerts runs as, and the runners job (id-aksmanager-runners-job), which only installs the runners and makes no role assignments.

Scopes: aks-subscriptions = this subscription and AKS_SUBSCRIPTIONS; identity-subscriptions = those, every subscription with a public zone, and shared services; container-registry and runners-environment are skipped when CONTAINER_REGISTRY_NAME / RUNNERS_ENVIRONMENT_ID are not set; secret:arc-app and secret:arc-app-key are skipped until the ARC GitHub App is installed from Settings.
Setup only adds. Removing a line here does not remove a grant already made: delete it in the portal or with az role assignment delete.

grants.why: Creates and changes clusters, their resource groups, managed identities, the Traefik NIC and node pools; joins the node subnet

grants.role: Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin
grants.why: kubectl on the clusters: the runners sign in through Entra (kubelogin), and on an Azure RBAC cluster Contributor gives no access inside it. A cluster using Kubernetes RBAC with Entra needs the identity in its admin group instead
The cluster identities (ASO's and the platform identities) made by bootstrap-cluster-identities.yml
secret-write.yml, secret-read.yml and secret-delete.yml; the create's Argo CD admin password and ASO client ID
Terraform state of the create's stages and the cluster identities (tfstate-identities)

may_assign.why: The create gives the cluster's own identities their roles, and identities and grants made through the CD repo get theirs. An ABAC condition limits it to these roles, to service principals only; it can never grant Owner, Contributor or any other role

grants.why: The runners' Container Apps and jobs (rg-aksmanager-runners only, so it cannot change its own job or the certificate job)
Placing the runners in the cluster monitor's Container Apps environment
The bootstrap GitHub App, to clone this repo and read its variables
The organisation's ARC GitHub App, which registers the runners
Writes (never reads) the copy of the App's key that the scaler (KEDA) reads
